stories.text: John Boot opened a herbalist's shop on Goose Gate in 1849, and his son Jesse was born in the area, into poverty, the next year.[^boots] After John died in 1860 his widow Mary kept the shop going as M & J Boot.[^boots] Jesse became a partner at 21, and in 1883 he built a larger store on the same site, the first of the Boots shops; Nottingham Civic Society put up a plaque here in 2015.[^boots]

stories.text: Built from 1854 to designs by Thomas Chambers Hine for Thomas Adams, a Quaker lace manufacturer, and opened in 1855 as his lace showroom and warehouse, with a chapel for the workers in the basement. Inspectors thought it a model example of its kind; since 1999 it has been part of Nottingham College.
The lace manufacturer Thomas Adams built this showroom and warehouse; it is named after him.[^s1][^s2]
The Nottingham architect Thomas Chambers Hine designed this lace showroom and warehouse.[^s1][^s2]

74534.sum: The Adams Building, formerly the Adams and Page warehouse on Stoney Street, is the largest building in the Lace Market district of the city of Nottingham in England. stories.text: The ice dancers Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean come from Nottingham.[^s1][^s2][^s3] The square outside the ice centre is named Bolero Square after their Olympic routine.[^s1][^s2][^s3] Jayne Torvill was born in Clifton on 7 October 1957 and worked as an insurance clerk at Norwich Union before skating full-time; at Sarajevo in 1984 she and Christopher Dean won the gold with their free dance to Ravel's Boléro, which earned twelve perfect 6.0 marks.[^s3]

74549.sum: The National Ice Centre is located in Nottingham, England. It is situated just east of the city centre, close to the historic Lace Market area. The NIC was the first twin Olympic-sized ice pad facility in the UK, "heralding a new era in the development of ice skating".

stories.text: The building began in 1839 as a grand Wesleyan chapel on Broad Street. Broadway opened here in 1990, and one of its screens is the only cinema screen designed by Sir Paul Smith.

Hockley has a taste for small cinema. Broadway was the first cinema in the UK to show Quentin Tarantino's Pulp Fiction, and from 2002 to 2011 the district also had The Screen Room, then the smallest commercial cinema in the world.

74666.sum: Broadway Cinema is an independent cinema and registered charity in Nottingham, England, located in the Hockley area of the city's Creative Quarter.
